entry_state: Replication prices the top-up at 9 while the supplied physical expected payment is 4.5. Separate mortality and risk-adjustment inputs complete the conditional insurance case; all four outcomes reconcile cash and profit. The variable-fee method now expands those service and finance distinctions.
exit_state: Variable-fee changes distinguish pass-through value, unearned service and permitted mitigation. Partial reinsurance recovers only the allocated covered loss; later changes affect both groups without duplicate component entries. A changed contract requires its own derecognition and replacement-value analysis.
findings: The 20 pool increase includes unearned fee 4, so the liability increases by 20 rather than only the policyholder share 16.
Adverse costs consume CSM before loss; reversal restores loss before margin. Risk mitigation changes recognition timing under prior documented conditions.
Only covered loss 8 supports initial recovery 4; applying 50 percent to total loss 20 would overstate equity by 6.
A covered-claim revision raises company equity by 2 and ends at cash 31.5 after service. The component cap does not create another recovery posting. No new defect observed.
